units.leftText: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God—
units.rightText: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,

units.leftText: the gospel He promised beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures,
units.rightText: which he promised afore through his prophets in the holy scriptures,

units.leftText: regarding His Son, who was a descendant of David according to the flesh,
units.rightText: concerning his Son, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh,

units.leftText: and who through the Spirit of holiness was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.
units.rightText: who was declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead; even Jesus Christ our Lord,

units.leftText: Through Him and on behalf of His name, we received grace and apostleship to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith.
units.rightText: through whom we received grace and apostleship, unto obedience of faith among all the nations, for his name’s sake;

units.leftText: And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: among whom are ye also, called to be Jesus Christ’s:

units.leftText: To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Unashamed of the Gospel
units.rightText: to all that are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed all over the world.
units.rightText: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world.

units.leftText: God, whom I serve with my spirit in preaching the gospel of His Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you
units.rightText: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you, always in my prayers

units.leftText: in my prayers at all times, asking that now at last by God’s will I may succeed in coming to you.
units.rightText: making request, if by any means now at length I may be prospered by the will of God to come unto you.

units.leftText: For I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you,
units.rightText: For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established;

units.leftText: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.
units.rightText: that is, that I with you may be comforted in you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine.

units.leftText: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, how often I planned to come to you (but have been prevented from visiting until now), in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.
units.rightText: And I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you (and was hindered hitherto), that I might have some fruit in you also, even as in the rest of the Gentiles.

units.leftText: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.
units.rightText: I am debtor both to Greeks and to Barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish.

units.leftText: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
units.rightText: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you also that are in Rome.

units.leftText: I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jew, then to the Greek.
units.rightText: For I am not ashamed of the gospel: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

units.leftText: For the gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish, just as it is written: “The righteous will live by faith.” God’s Wrath against Sin
units.rightText: For therein is revealed a righteousness of God from faith unto faith: as it is written, But the righteous shall live by faith.
leftNotes: 1:17 Literally For in it is revealed the righteousness of God from faith to faith

units.leftText: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness.
units.rightText: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hinder the truth in unrighteousness;

units.leftText: For what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.
units.rightText: because that which is known of God is manifest in them; for God manifested it unto them.

units.leftText: For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood from His workmanship, so that men are without excuse.
units.rightText: For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divinity; that they may be without excuse:

units.leftText: For although they knew God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks to Him, but they became futile in their thinking and darkened in their foolish hearts.
units.rightText: because that, knowing God, they glorified him not as God, neither gave thanks; but became vain in their reasonings, and their senseless heart was darkened.

units.leftText: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools,
units.rightText: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

units.leftText: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles.
units.rightText: and changed the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, and four-footed beasts, and creeping things.

units.leftText: Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity for the dishonoring of their bodies with one another.
units.rightText: Wherefore God gave them up in the lusts of their hearts unto uncleanness, that their bodies should be dishonored among themselves:

units.leftText: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is forever worthy of praise! Amen.
units.rightText: for that they exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshipped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.

units.leftText: For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.
units.rightText: For this cause God gave them up unto vile passions: for their women changed the natural use into that which is against nature:

units.leftText: Likewise, the men abandoned natural relations with women and burned with lust for one another. Men committed indecent acts with other men and received in themselves the due penalty for their error.
units.rightText: and likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another, men with men working unseemliness, and receiving in themselves that recompense of their error which was due.

units.leftText: Furthermore, since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, He gave them up to a depraved mind, to do what ought not to be done.
units.rightText: And even as they refused to have God in their knowledge, God gave them up unto a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not fitting;

units.leftText: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed, and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and malice. They are gossips,
units.rightText: being filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malignity; whisperers,

units.leftText: slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, and boastful. They invent new forms of evil; they disobey their parents.
units.rightText: backbiters, hateful to God, insolent, haughty, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,

units.leftText: They are senseless, faithless, heartless, merciless.
units.rightText: without understanding, covenant-breakers, without natural affection, unmerciful:

units.leftText: Although they know God’s righteous decree that those who do such things are worthy of death, they not only continue to do these things, but also approve of those who practice them.
units.rightText: who, knowing the ordinance of God, that they that practise such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but also consent with them that practise them.

units.leftText: You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on another. For on whatever grounds you judge the other, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.
units.rightText: Wherefore thou art without excuse, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest: for wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest dost practise the same things.

units.leftText: And we know that God’s judgment against those who do such things is based on truth.
units.rightText: And we know that the judgment of God is according to truth against them that practise such things.

units.leftText: So when you, O man, pass judgment on others, yet do the same things, do you think you will escape God’s judgment?
units.rightText: And reckonest thou this, O man, who judgest them that practise such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?

units.leftText: Or do you disregard the riches of His kindness, tolerance, and patience, not realizing that God’s kindness leads you to repentance?
units.rightText: Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering, not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?

units.leftText: But because of your hard and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of wrath, when God’s righteous judgment will be revealed.
units.rightText: but after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up for thyself wrath in the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God;

units.leftText: God “will repay each one according to his deeds.”
units.rightText: who will render to every man according to his works:

units.leftText: To those who by perseverance in doing good seek glory, honor, and immortality, He will give eternal life.
units.rightText: to them that by patience in well-doing seek for glory and honor and incorruption, eternal life:

units.leftText: But for those who are self-seeking and who reject the truth and follow wickedness, there will be wrath and anger.
units.rightText: but unto them that are factious, and obey not the truth, but obey unrighteousness, shall be wrath and indignation,

units.leftText: There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil, first for the Jew, then for the Greek;
units.rightText: tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that worketh evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Greek;

units.leftText: but glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does good, first for the Jew, then for the Greek.
units.rightText: but glory and honor and peace to every man that worketh good, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek:

units.leftText: For God does not show favoritism.
units.rightText: for there is no respect of persons with God.

units.leftText: All who sin apart from the law will also perish apart from the law, and all who sin under the law will be judged by the law.
units.rightText: For as many as have sinned without the law shall also perish without the law: and as many as have sinned under the law shall be judged by the law;

units.leftText: For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but it is the doers of the law who will be declared righteous.
units.rightText: for not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified;

units.leftText: Indeed, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law.
units.rightText: (for when Gentiles that have not the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are the law unto themselves;

units.leftText: So they show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, their consciences also bearing witness, and their thoughts either accusing or defending them
units.rightText: in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness therewith, and their thoughts one with another accusing or else excusing them);

units.leftText: on the day when God will judge men’s secrets through Christ Jesus, as proclaimed by my gospel. The Jews and the Law
units.rightText: in the day when God shall judge the secrets of men, according to my gospel, by Jesus Christ.
leftNotes: 2:16 BYZ and TR through Jesus Christ

units.leftText: Now you, if you call yourself a Jew; if you rely on the law and boast in God;
units.rightText: But if thou bearest the name of a Jew, and restest upon the law, and gloriest in God,

units.leftText: if you know His will and approve of what is superior because you are instructed by the law;
units.rightText: and knowest his will, and approvest the things that are excellent, being instructed out of the law,

units.leftText: if you are convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light for those in darkness,
units.rightText: and art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them that are in darkness,

units.leftText: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, because you have in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth —
units.rightText: a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of babes, having in the law the form of knowledge and of the truth;

units.leftText: you, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?
units.rightText: thou therefore that teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal?

units.leftText: You who forbid adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
units.rightText: thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou rob temples?

units.leftText: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
units.rightText: thou who gloriest in the law, through thy transgression of the law dishonorest thou God?

units.leftText: As it is written: “God’s name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”
units.rightText: For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you, even as it is written.

units.leftText: Circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
units.rightText: For circumcision indeed profiteth, if thou be a doer of the law: but if thou be a transgressor of the law, thy circumcision is become uncircumcision.

units.leftText: If a man who is not circumcised keeps the requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision?
units.rightText: If therefore the uncircumcision keep the ordinances of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be reckoned for circumcision?

units.leftText: The one who is physically uncircumcised yet keeps the law will condemn you who, even though you have the written code and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.
units.rightText: and shall not the uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge thee, who with the letter and circumcision art a transgressor of the law?

units.leftText: A man is not a Jew because he is one outwardly, nor is circumcision only outward and physical.
units.rightText: For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh:

units.leftText: No, a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. Such a man’s praise does not come from men, but from God.
units.rightText: but he is a Jew who is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.

units.leftText: What, then, is the advantage of being a Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision?
units.rightText: What advantage then hath the Jew? or what is the profit of circumcision?

units.leftText: Much in every way. First of all, they have been entrusted with the very words of God.
units.rightText: Much every way: first of all, that they were intrusted with the oracles of God.

units.leftText: What if some did not have faith? Will their lack of faith nullify God’s faithfulness?
units.rightText: For what if some were without faith? shall their want of faith make of none effect the faithfulness of God?

units.leftText: Certainly not! Let God be true and every man a liar. As it is written: “So that You may be proved right when You speak and victorious when You judge.”
units.rightText: God forbid: yea, let God be found true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That thou mightest be justified in thy words, And mightest prevail when thou comest into judgment.
leftNotes: 3:4 Or when You are judged; Psalm 51:4|PSA 51:4* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: But if our unrighteousness highlights the righteousness of God, what shall we say? That God is unjust to inflict His wrath on us? I am speaking in human terms.
units.rightText: But if our unrighteousness commendeth the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous who visiteth with wrath? (I speak after the manner of men.)

units.leftText: Certainly not! In that case, how could God judge the world?
units.rightText: God forbid: for then how shall God judge the world?

units.leftText: However, if my falsehood accentuates God’s truthfulness, to the increase of His glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?
units.rightText: But if the truth of God through my lie abounded unto his glory, why am I also still judged as a sinner?

units.leftText: Why not say, as some slanderously claim that we say, “Let us do evil that good may result”? Their condemnation is deserved! There Is No One Righteous (Psalm 14:1–7|PSA 14:1-7*; Psalm 53:1–6|PSA 53:1-6*; Isaiah 59:1–17|ISA 59:1-17*)
units.rightText: and why not (as we are slanderously reported, and as some affirm that we say), Let us do evil, that good may come? whose condemnation is just.

units.leftText: What then? Are we any better? Not at all. For we have already made the charge that Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin.
units.rightText: What then? are we better than they? No, in no wise: for we before laid to the charge both of Jews and Greeks, that they are all under sin;

units.leftText: As it is written: “There is no one righteous, not even one.
units.rightText: as it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one;

units.leftText: There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God.
units.rightText: There is none that understandeth, There is none that seeketh after God;

units.leftText: All have turned away, they have together become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.”
units.rightText: They have all turned aside, they are together become unprofitable; There is none that doeth good, no, not so much as one:

units.leftText: “Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit.” “The venom of vipers is on their lips.”
units.rightText: Their throat is an open sepulchre; With their tongues they have used deceit: The poison of asps is under their lips:

units.leftText: “Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness.”
units.rightText: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness:

units.leftText: “Their feet are swift to shed blood;
units.rightText: Their feet are swift to shed blood;

units.leftText: ruin and misery lie in their wake,
units.rightText: Destruction and misery are in their ways;

units.leftText: and the way of peace they have not known.”
units.rightText: And the way of peace have they not known:

units.leftText: “There is no fear of God before their eyes.”
units.rightText: There is no fear of God before their eyes.

units.leftText: Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.
units.rightText: Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it speaketh to them that are under the law; that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may be brought under the judgment of God:

units.leftText: Therefore no one will be justified in His sight by works of the law. For the law merely brings awareness of sin. Righteousness through Faith in Christ (Philippians 3:1–11|PHP 3:1-11*)
units.rightText: because by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified in his sight; for through the law cometh the knowledge of sin.

units.leftText: But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, as attested by the Law and the Prophets.
units.rightText: But now apart from the law a righteousness of God hath been manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets;

units.leftText: And this righteousness from God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe. There is no distinction,
units.rightText: even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ unto all them that believe; for there is no distinction;

units.leftText: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
units.rightText: for all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God;

units.leftText: and are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:

units.leftText: God presented Him as an atoning sacrifice in His blood through faith, in order to demonstrate His righteousness, because in His forbearance He had passed over the sins committed beforehand.
units.rightText: whom God set forth to be a propitiation, through faith, in his blood, to show his righteousness because of the passing over of the sins done aforetime, in the forbearance of God;

units.leftText: He did this to demonstrate His righteousness at the present time, so as to be just and to justify the one who has faith in Jesus.
units.rightText: for the showing, I say, of his righteousness at this present season: that he might himself be just, and the justifier of him that hath faith in Jesus.

units.leftText: Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. On what principle? On that of works? No, but on that of faith.
units.rightText: Where then is the glorying? It is excluded. By what manner of law? of works? Nay: but by a law of faith.

units.leftText: For we maintain that a man is justified by faith apart from works of the law.
units.rightText: We reckon therefore that a man is justified by faith apart from the works of the law.

units.leftText: Is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles too? Yes, of Gentiles too,
units.rightText: Or is God the God of Jews only? is he not the God of Gentiles also? Yea, of Gentiles also:

units.leftText: since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith.
units.rightText: if so be that God is one, and he shall justify the circumcision by faith, and the uncircumcision through faith.

units.leftText: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law.
units.rightText: Do we then make the law of none effect through faith? God forbid: nay, we establish the law.

units.leftText: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has discovered?
units.rightText: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather, hath found according to the flesh?

units.leftText: If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God.
units.rightText: For if Abraham was justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not toward God.

units.leftText: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
units.rightText: For what saith the scripture? And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned unto him for righteousness.

units.leftText: Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.
units.rightText: Now to him that worketh, the reward is not reckoned as of grace, but as of debt.

units.leftText: However, to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is credited as righteousness.
units.rightText: But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is reckoned for righteousness.

units.leftText: And David speaks likewise of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:
units.rightText: Even as David also pronounceth blessing upon the man, unto whom God reckoneth righteousness apart from works,

units.leftText: “Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
units.rightText: saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, And whose sins are covered.

units.leftText: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him.”
units.rightText: Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not reckon sin.

units.leftText: Is this blessing only on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness.
units.rightText: Is this blessing then pronounced upon the circumcision, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say, To Abraham his faith was reckoned for righteousness.

units.leftText: In what context was it credited? Was it after his circumcision, or before? It was not after, but before.
units.rightText: How then was it reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision:
leftNotes: 4:10 Literally How then was it reckoned—being in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

units.leftText: And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but are not circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.
units.rightText: and he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had while he was in uncircumcision: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be in uncircumcision, that righteousness might be reckoned unto them;

units.leftText: And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised. Abraham Receives the Promise (Genesis 15:8–21|GEN 15:8-21*)
units.rightText: and the father of circumcision to them who not only are of the circumcision, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham which he had in uncircumcision.

units.leftText: For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not given through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.
units.rightText: For not through the law was the promise to Abraham or to his seed that he should be heir of the world, but through the righteousness of faith.

units.leftText: For if those who live by the law are heirs, faith is useless and the promise is worthless,
units.rightText: For if they that are of the law are heirs, faith is made void, and the promise is made of none effect:

units.leftText: because the law brings wrath. And where there is no law, there is no transgression.
units.rightText: for the law worketh wrath; but where there is no law, neither is there transgression.

units.leftText: Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring — not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.
units.rightText: For this cause it is of faith, that it may be according to grace; to the end that the promise may be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all

units.leftText: As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” He is our father in the presence of God, in whom he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not yet exist.
units.rightText: (as it is written, A father of many nations have I made thee) before him whom he believed, even God, who giveth life to the dead, and calleth the things that are not, as though they were.

units.leftText: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as he had been told, “So shall your offspring be.”
units.rightText: Who in hope believed against hope, to the end that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken, So shall thy seed be.

units.leftText: Without weakening in his faith, he acknowledged the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old) and the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb.
units.rightText: And without being weakened in faith he considered his own body now as good as dead (he being about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah’s womb;

units.leftText: Yet he did not waver through disbelief in the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God,
units.rightText: yet, looking unto the promise of God, he wavered not through unbelief, but waxed strong through faith, giving glory to God,

units.leftText: being fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised.
units.rightText: and being fully assured that what he had promised, he was able also to perform.

units.leftText: This is why “it was credited to him as righteousness.”
units.rightText: Wherefore also it was reckoned unto him for righteousness.

units.leftText: Now the words “it was credited to him” were written not only for Abraham,
units.rightText: Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was reckoned unto him;

units.leftText: but also for us, to whom righteousness will be credited— for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
units.rightText: but for our sake also, unto whom it shall be reckoned, who believe on him that raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,

units.leftText: He was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification.
units.rightText: who was delivered up for our trespasses, and was raised for our justification.

units.leftText: Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
units.rightText: Being therefore justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ;

units.leftText: through whom we have gained access by faith into this grace in which we stand. And we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God.
units.rightText: through whom also we have had our access by faith into this grace wherein we stand; and we rejoice in hope of the glory of God.
leftNotes: 5:2 Or exult; also in verses 3 and 11

units.leftText: Not only that, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance;
units.rightText: And not only so, but we also rejoice in our tribulations: knowing that tribulation worketh stedfastness;

units.leftText: perseverance, character; and character, hope.
units.rightText: and stedfastness, approvedness; and approvedness, hope:

units.leftText: And hope does not disappoint us, because God has poured out His love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, whom He has given us. Christ’s Sacrifice for the Ungodly (John 3:1–21|JHN 3:1-21*)
units.rightText: and hope putteth not to shame; because the love of God hath been shed abroad in our hearts through the Holy Spirit which was given unto us.

units.leftText: For at just the right time, while we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.
units.rightText: For while we were yet weak, in due season Christ died for the ungodly.

units.leftText: Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous man, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die.
units.rightText: For scarcely for a righteous man will one die: for peradventure for the good man some one would even dare to die.

units.leftText: But God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
units.rightText: But God commendeth his own love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

units.leftText: Therefore, since we have now been justified by His blood, how much more shall we be saved from wrath through Him!
units.rightText: Much more then, being now justified by his blood, shall we be saved from the wrath of God through him.

units.leftText: For if, when we were enemies of God, we were reconciled to Him through the death of His Son, how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved through His life!
units.rightText: For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, shall we be saved by his life;

units.leftText: Not only that, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation. Death in Adam, Life in Christ (Genesis 3:1–7|GEN 3:1-7*)
units.rightText: and not only so, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.

units.leftText: Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death was passed on to all men, because all sinned.
units.rightText: Therefore, as through one man sin entered into the world, and death through sin; and so death passed unto all men, for that all sinned:—

units.leftText: For sin was in the world before the law was given; but sin is not taken into account when there is no law.
units.rightText: for until the law sin was in the world; but sin is not imputed when there is no law.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed. He is a pattern of the One to come.
units.rightText: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the likeness of Adam’s transgression, who is a figure of him that was to come.

units.leftText: But the gift is not like the trespass. For if the many died by the trespass of the one man, how much more did God’s grace and the gift that came by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many!
units.rightText: But not as the trespass, so also is the free gift. For if by the trespass of the one the many died, much more did the grace of God, and the gift by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound unto the many.

units.leftText: Again, the gift is not like the result of the one man’s sin: The judgment that followed one sin brought condemnation, but the gift that followed many trespasses brought justification.
units.rightText: And not as through one that sinned, so is the gift: for the judgment came of one unto condemnation, but the free gift came of many trespasses unto justification.

units.leftText: For if, by the trespass of the one man, death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!
units.rightText: For if, by the trespass of the one, death reigned through the one; much more shall they that receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one, even Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: So then, just as one trespass brought condemnation for all men, so also one act of righteousness brought justification and life for all men.
units.rightText: So then as through one trespass the judgment came unto all men to condemnation; even so through one act of righteousness the free gift came unto all men to justification of life.

units.leftText: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.
units.rightText: For as through the one man’s disobedience the many were made sinners, even so through the obedience of the one shall the many be made righteous.

units.leftText: The law came in so that the trespass would increase; but where sin increased, grace increased all the more,
units.rightText: And the law came in besides, that the trespass might abound; but where sin abounded, grace did abound more exceedingly:

units.leftText: so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
units.rightText: that, as sin reigned in death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

units.leftText: What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?
units.rightText: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?

units.leftText: Certainly not! How can we who died to sin live in it any longer?
units.rightText: God forbid. We who died to sin, how shall we any longer live therein?

units.leftText: Or aren’t you aware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?
units.rightText: Or are ye ignorant that all we who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?

units.leftText: We were therefore buried with Him through baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may walk in newness of life.
units.rightText: We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.

units.leftText: For if we have been united with Him like this in His death, we will certainly also be united with Him in His resurrection.
units.rightText: For if we have become united with him in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection;

units.leftText: We know that our old self was crucified with Him so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, that we should no longer be slaves to sin.
units.rightText: knowing this, that our old man was crucified with him, that the body of sin might be done away, that so we should no longer be in bondage to sin;

units.leftText: For anyone who has died has been freed from sin.
units.rightText: for he that hath died is justified from sin.

units.leftText: Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him.
units.rightText: But if we died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him;

units.leftText: For we know that since Christ was raised from the dead, He cannot die again; death no longer has dominion over Him.
units.rightText: knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death no more hath dominion over him.

units.leftText: The death He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life He lives, He lives to God.
units.rightText: For the death that he died, he died unto sin once: but the life that he liveth, he liveth unto God.

units.leftText: So you too must count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: Even so reckon ye also yourselves to be dead unto sin, but alive unto God in Christ Jesus.

units.leftText: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires.
units.rightText: Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey the lusts thereof:

units.leftText: Do not present the parts of your body to sin as instruments of wickedness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life; and present the parts of your body to Him as instruments of righteousness.
units.rightText: neither present your members unto sin as instruments of unrighteousness; but present yourselves unto God, as alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.

units.leftText: For sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace. The Wages of Sin
units.rightText: For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under law, but under grace.

units.leftText: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? Certainly not!
units.rightText: What then? shall we sin, because we are not under law, but under grace? God forbid.

units.leftText: Do you not know that when you offer yourselves as obedient slaves, you are slaves to the one you obey, whether you are slaves to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness?
units.rightText: Know ye not, that to whom ye present yourselves as servants unto obedience, his servants ye are whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?

units.leftText: But thanks be to God that, though you once were slaves to sin, you wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were committed.
units.rightText: But thanks be to God, that, whereas ye were servants of sin, ye became obedient from the heart to that form of teaching whereunto ye were delivered;

units.leftText: You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.
units.rightText: and being made free from sin, ye became servants of righteousness.

units.leftText: I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity and to escalating wickedness, so now offer them in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness.
units.rightText: I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity of your flesh: for as ye presented your members as servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity, even so now present your members as servants to righteousness unto sanctification.

units.leftText: For when you were slaves to sin, you were free of obligation to righteousness.
units.rightText: For when ye were servants of sin, ye were free in regard of righteousness.

units.leftText: What fruit did you reap at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The outcome of those things is death.
units.rightText: What fruit then had ye at that time in the things whereof ye are now ashamed? for the end of those things is death.

units.leftText: But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, the fruit you reap leads to holiness, and the outcome is eternal life.
units.rightText: But now being made free from sin and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto sanctification, and the end eternal life.

units.leftText: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
units.rightText: For the wages of sin is death; but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.leftText: Do you not know, brothers (for I am speaking to those who know the law), that the law has authority over a man only as long as he lives?
units.rightText: Or are ye ignorant, brethren (for I speak to men who know the law), that the law hath dominion over a man for so long time as he liveth?

units.leftText: For instance, a married woman is bound by law to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is released from the law of marriage.
units.rightText: For the woman that hath a husband is bound by law to the husband while he liveth; but if the husband die, she is discharged from the law of the husband.

units.leftText: So then, if she is joined to another man while her husband is still alive, she is called an adulteress; but if her husband dies, she is free from that law and is not an adulteress if she marries another man.
units.rightText: So then if, while the husband liveth, she be joined to another man, she shall be called an adulteress: but if the husband die, she is free from the law, so that she is no adulteress, though she be joined to another man.

units.leftText: Therefore, my brothers, you also died to the law through the body of Christ, that you might belong to another, to Him who was raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit to God.
units.rightText: Wherefore, my brethren, ye also were made dead to the law through the body of Christ; that ye should be joined to another, even to him who was raised from the dead, that we might bring forth fruit unto God.

units.leftText: For when we lived according to the flesh, the sinful passions aroused by the law were at work in our bodies, bearing fruit for death.
units.rightText: For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions, which were through the law, wrought in our members to bring forth fruit unto death.

units.leftText: But now, having died to what bound us, we have been released from the law, so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit, and not in the old way of the written code. God’s Law Is Holy
units.rightText: But now we have been discharged from the law, having died to that wherein we were held; so that we serve in newness of the spirit, and not in oldness of the letter.

units.leftText: What then shall we say? Is the law sin? Certainly not! Indeed, I would not have been mindful of sin if not for the law. For I would not have been aware of coveting if the law had not said, “Do not covet.”
units.rightText: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Howbeit, I had not known sin, except through the law: for I had not known coveting, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet:

units.leftText: But sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every kind of covetous desire. For apart from the law, sin is dead.
units.rightText: but sin, finding occasion, wrought in me through the commandment all manner of coveting: for apart from the law sin is dead.

units.leftText: Once I was alive apart from the law; but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life and I died.
units.rightText: And I was alive apart from the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died;

units.leftText: So I discovered that the very commandment that was meant to bring life actually brought death.
units.rightText: and the commandment, which was unto life, this I found to be unto death:

units.leftText: For sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through the commandment put me to death.
units.rightText: for sin, finding occasion, through the commandment beguiled me, and through it slew me.

units.leftText: So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good. Struggling with Sin
units.rightText: So that the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and righteous, and good.

units.leftText: Did that which is good, then, become death to me? Certainly not! But in order that sin might be exposed as sin, it produced death in me through what was good, so that through the commandment sin might become utterly sinful.
units.rightText: Did then that which is good become death unto me? God forbid. But sin, that it might be shown to be sin, by working death to me through that which is good;—that through the commandment sin might become exceeding sinful.

units.leftText: We know that the law is spiritual; but I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.
units.rightText: For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.

units.leftText: I do not understand what I do. For what I want to do, I do not do. But what I hate, I do.
units.rightText: For that which I do I know not: for not what I would, that do I practise; but what I hate, that I do.

units.leftText: And if I do what I do not want to do, I admit that the law is good.
units.rightText: But if what I would not, that I do, I consent unto the law that it is good.

units.leftText: In that case, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.
units.rightText: So now it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwelleth in me.

units.leftText: I know that nothing good lives in me, that is, in my flesh; for I have the desire to do what is good, but I cannot carry it out.
units.rightText: For I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, dwelleth no good thing: for to will is present with me, but to do that which is good is not.

units.leftText: For I do not do the good I want to do. Instead, I keep on doing the evil I do not want to do.
units.rightText: For the good which I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I practise.

units.leftText: And if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.
units.rightText: But if what I would not, that I do, it is no more I that do it, but sin which dwelleth in me.

units.leftText: So this is the principle I have discovered: When I want to do good, evil is right there with me.
units.rightText: I find then the law, that, to me who would do good, evil is present.

units.leftText: For in my inner being I delight in God’s law.
units.rightText: For I delight in the law of God after the inward man:

units.leftText: But I see another law at work in my body, warring against the law of my mind and holding me captive to the law of sin that dwells within me.
units.rightText: but I see a different law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity under the law of sin which is in my members.
leftNotes: 7:23 Literally captive to the law of sin being in my members.

units.leftText: What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?
units.rightText: Wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me out of the body of this death?

units.leftText: Thanks be to God, through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, with my mind I serve the law of God, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin.
units.rightText: I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then I of myself with the mind, indeed, serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.

units.leftText: Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
units.rightText: There is therefore now no condemnation to them that are in Christ Jesus.
leftNotes: 8:1 BYZ and TR in Christ Jesus, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.

units.leftText: For in Christ Jesus the law of the Spirit of life set you free from the law of sin and death.
units.rightText: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free from the law of sin and of death.

units.leftText: For what the law was powerless to do in that it was weakened by the flesh, God did by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin. He thus condemned sin in the flesh,
units.rightText: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God, sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh:
leftNotes: 8:3 Literally in the likeness of sinful flesh and for sin

units.leftText: so that the righteous standard of the law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.
units.rightText: that the ordinance of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

units.leftText: Those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh; but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.
units.rightText: For they that are after the flesh mind the things of the flesh; but they that are after the Spirit the things of the Spirit.

units.leftText: The mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace,
units.rightText: For the mind of the flesh is death; but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace:

units.leftText: because the mind of the flesh is hostile to God: It does not submit to God’s law, nor can it do so.
units.rightText: because the mind of the flesh is enmity against God; for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can it be:

units.leftText: Those controlled by the flesh cannot please God.
units.rightText: and they that are in the flesh cannot please God.
leftNotes: 8:8 Literally Those being in the flesh; similarly in verse 9

units.leftText: You, however, are controlled not by the flesh, but by the Spirit, if the Spirit of God lives in you. And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ.
units.rightText: But ye are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you. But if any man hath not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.

units.leftText: But if Christ is in you, your body is dead because of sin, yet your spirit is alive because of righteousness.
units.rightText: And if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin; but the spirit is life because of righteousness.
leftNotes: 8:10 Or yet the Spirit is life

units.leftText: And if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead is living in you, He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit, who lives in you. Heirs with Christ
units.rightText: But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwelleth in you, he that raised up Christ Jesus from the dead shall give life also to your mortal bodies through his Spirit that dwelleth in you.
leftNotes: 8:11 NA, BYZ, and TR raised Christ from the dead

units.leftText: Therefore, brothers, we have an obligation, but it is not to the flesh, to live according to it.
units.rightText: So then, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live after the flesh:

units.leftText: For if you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
units.rightText: for if ye live after the flesh, ye must die; but if by the Spirit ye put to death the deeds of the body, ye shall live.

units.leftText: For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.
units.rightText: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God.

units.leftText: For you did not receive a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption to sonship, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”
units.rightText: For ye received not the spirit of bondage again unto fear; but ye received the spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.

units.leftText: The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.
units.rightText: The Spirit himself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are children of God:

units.leftText: And if we are children, then we are heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ — if indeed we suffer with Him, so that we may also be glorified with Him. Future Glory (2 Corinthians 5:1–10|2CO 5:1-10*)
units.rightText: and if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified with him.

units.leftText: I consider that our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us.
units.rightText: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed to us-ward.

units.leftText: The creation waits in eager expectation for the revelation of the sons of God.
units.rightText: For the earnest expectation of the creation waiteth for the revealing of the sons of God.

units.leftText: For the creation was subjected to futility, not by its own will, but because of the One who subjected it, in hope
units.rightText: For the creation was subjected to vanity, not of its own will, but by reason of him who subjected it, in hope

units.leftText: that the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to decay and brought into the glorious freedom of the children of God.
units.rightText: that the creation itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.

units.leftText: We know that the whole creation has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth until the present time.
units.rightText: For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.

units.leftText: Not only that, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for our adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies.
units.rightText: And not only so, but ourselves also, who have the first-fruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for our adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.

units.leftText: For in this hope we were saved; but hope that is seen is no hope at all. Who hopes for what he can already see?
units.rightText: For in hope were we saved: but hope that is seen is not hope: for who hopeth for that which he seeth?

units.leftText: But if we hope for what we do not yet see, we wait for it patiently.
units.rightText: But if we hope for that which we see not, then do we with patience wait for it.

units.leftText: In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words.
units.rightText: And in like manner the Spirit also helpeth our infirmity: for we know not how to pray as we ought; but the Spirit himself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered;

units.leftText: And He who searches our hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God. God Works in All Things (Ephesians 1:3–14|EPH 1:3-14*)
units.rightText: and he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.

units.leftText: And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose.
units.rightText: And we know that to them that love God all things work together for good, even to them that are called according to his purpose.

units.leftText: For those God foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers.
units.rightText: For whom he foreknew, he also foreordained to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren:

units.leftText: And those He predestined, He also called; those He called, He also justified; those He justified, He also glorified.
units.rightText: and whom he foreordained, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified.

units.leftText: What then shall we say in response to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
units.rightText: What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?

units.leftText: He who did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?
units.rightText: He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not also with him freely give us all things?

units.leftText: Who will bring any charge against God’s elect? It is God who justifies.
units.rightText: Who shall lay anything to the charge of God’s elect? It is God that justifieth;

units.leftText: Who is there to condemn us? For Christ Jesus, who died, and more than that was raised to life, is at the right hand of God— and He is interceding for us. More than Conquerors (Psalm 44:1–26|PSA 44:1-26*)
units.rightText: who is he that condemneth? It is Christ Jesus that died, yea rather, that was raised from the dead, who is at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us.

units.leftText: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall trouble or distress or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?
units.rightText: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or anguish, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?

units.leftText: As it is written: “For Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.”
units.rightText: Even as it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; We were accounted as sheep for the slaughter.

units.leftText: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.
units.rightText: Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.

units.leftText: For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers,
units.rightText: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,

units.leftText: neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
units.rightText: nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.leftText: I speak the truth in Christ; I am not lying, as confirmed by my conscience in the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience bearing witness with me in the Holy Spirit,

units.leftText: I have deep sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.
units.rightText: that I have great sorrow and unceasing pain in my heart.

units.leftText: For I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my own flesh and blood,
units.rightText: For I could wish that I myself were anathema from Christ for my brethren’s sake, my kinsmen according to the flesh:

units.leftText: the people of Israel. Theirs is the adoption as sons; theirs the divine glory and the covenants; theirs the giving of the law, the temple worship, and the promises.
units.rightText: who are Israelites; whose is the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises;

units.leftText: Theirs are the patriarchs, and from them proceeds the human descent of Christ, who is God over all, forever worthy of praise! Amen. God’s Sovereign Choice (Genesis 25:19–28|GEN 25:19-28*; Malachi 1:1–5|MAL 1:1-5*)
units.rightText: whose are the fathers, and of whom is Christ as concerning the flesh, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.

units.leftText: It is not as though God’s word has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel.
units.rightText: But it is not as though the word of God hath come to nought. For they are not all Israel, that are of Israel:

units.leftText: Nor because they are Abraham’s descendants are they all his children. On the contrary, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”
units.rightText: neither, because they are Abraham’s seed, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called.

units.leftText: So it is not the children of the flesh who are God’s children, but it is the children of the promise who are regarded as offspring.
units.rightText: That is, it is not the children of the flesh that are children of God; but the children of the promise are reckoned for a seed.

units.leftText: For this is what the promise stated: “At the appointed time I will return, and Sarah will have a son.”
units.rightText: For this is a word of promise, According to this season will I come, and Sarah shall have a son.

units.leftText: Not only that, but Rebecca’s children were conceived by one man, our father Isaac.
units.rightText: And not only so; but Rebecca also having conceived by one, even by our father Isaac—

units.leftText: Yet before the twins were born or had done anything good or bad, in order that God’s plan of election might stand,
units.rightText: for the children being not yet born, neither having done anything good or bad, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth,

units.leftText: not by works but by Him who calls, she was told, “The older will serve the younger.”
units.rightText: it was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger.

units.leftText: So it is written: “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”
units.rightText: Even as it is written, Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.

units.leftText: What then shall we say? Is God unjust? Certainly not!
units.rightText: What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid.

units.leftText: For He says to Moses: “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”
units.rightText: For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.

units.leftText: So then, it does not depend on man’s desire or effort, but on God’s mercy.
units.rightText: So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that hath mercy.

units.leftText: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: “I raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power in you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”
units.rightText: For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, For this very purpose did I raise thee up, that I might show in thee my power, and that my name might be published abroad in all the earth.

units.leftText: Therefore God has mercy on whom He wants to have mercy, and He hardens whom He wants to harden.
units.rightText: So then he hath mercy on whom he will, and whom he will he hardeneth.

units.leftText: One of you will say to me, “Then why does God still find fault? For who can resist His will?”
units.rightText: Thou wilt say then unto me, Why doth he still find fault? For who withstandeth his will?

units.leftText: But who are you, O man, to talk back to God? Shall what is formed say to Him who formed it, “Why did You make me like this?”
units.rightText: Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why didst thou make me thus?

units.leftText: Does not the potter have the right to make from the same lump of clay one vessel for special occasions and another for common use?
units.rightText: Or hath not the potter a right over the clay, from the same lump to make one part a vessel unto honor, and another unto dishonor?

units.leftText: What if God, intending to show His wrath and make His power known, bore with great patience the vessels of His wrath, prepared for destruction?
units.rightText: What if God, willing to show his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering vessels of wrath fitted unto destruction:

units.leftText: What if He did this to make the riches of His glory known to the vessels of His mercy, whom He prepared in advance for glory —
units.rightText: and that he might make known the riches of his glory upon vessels of mercy, which he afore prepared unto glory,

units.leftText: including us, whom He has called not only from the Jews, but also from the Gentiles?
units.rightText: even us, whom he also called, not from the Jews only, but also from the Gentiles?

units.leftText: As He says in Hosea: “I will call them ‘My People’ who are not My people, and I will call her ‘My Beloved’ who is not My beloved,”
units.rightText: As he saith also in Hosea, I will call that my people, which was not my people; And her beloved, that was not beloved.

units.leftText: and, “It will happen that in the very place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’”
units.rightText: And it shall be, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, There shall they be called sons of the living God.

units.leftText: Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: “Though the number of the Israelites is like the sand of the sea, only the remnant will be saved.
units.rightText: And Isaiah crieth concerning Israel, If the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, it is the remnant that shall be saved:

units.leftText: For the Lord will carry out His sentence on the earth thoroughly and decisively.”
units.rightText: for the Lord will execute his word upon the earth, finishing it and cutting it short.

units.leftText: It is just as Isaiah foretold: “Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us descendants, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.” Israel’s Unbelief
units.rightText: And, as Isaiah hath said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, We had become as Sodom, and had been made like unto Gomorrah.

units.leftText: What then will we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained it, a righteousness that is by faith;
units.rightText: What shall we say then? That the Gentiles, who followed not after righteousness, attained to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith:

units.leftText: but Israel, who pursued a law of righteousness, has not attained it.
units.rightText: but Israel, following after a law of righteousness, did not arrive at that law.

units.leftText: Why not? Because their pursuit was not by faith, but as if it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone,
units.rightText: Wherefore? Because they sought it not by faith, but as it were by works. They stumbled at the stone of stumbling;

units.leftText: as it is written: “See, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
units.rightText: even as it is written, Behold, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence: And he that believeth on him shall not be put to shame.

units.leftText: Brothers, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for the Israelites is for their salvation.
units.rightText: Brethren, my heart’s desire and my supplication to God is for them, that they may be saved.

units.leftText: For I testify about them that they are zealous for God, but not on the basis of knowledge.
units.rightText: For I bear them witness that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.

units.leftText: Because they were ignorant of God’s righteousness and sought to establish their own, they did not submit to God’s righteousness.
units.rightText: For being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and seeking to establish their own, they did not subject themselves to the righteousness of God.

units.leftText: For Christ is the end of the law, to bring righteousness to everyone who believes.
units.rightText: For Christ is the end of the law unto righteousness to every one that believeth.

units.leftText: For concerning the righteousness that is by the law, Moses writes: “The man who does these things will live by them.”
units.rightText: For Moses writeth that the man that doeth the righteousness which is of the law shall live thereby.

units.leftText: But the righteousness that is by faith says: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’ (that is, to bring Christ down)
units.rightText: But the righteousness which is of faith saith thus, Say not in thy heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down:)

units.leftText: or, ‘Who will descend into the Abyss?’ (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).”
units.rightText: or, Who shall descend into the abyss? (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.)

units.leftText: But what does it say? “The word is near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart,” that is, the word of faith we are proclaiming:
units.rightText: But what saith it? The word is nigh thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach:

units.leftText: that if you confess with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.
units.rightText: because if thou shalt confess with thy mouth Jesus as Lord, and shalt believe in thy heart that God raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved:

units.leftText: For with your heart you believe and are justified, and with your mouth you confess and are saved.
units.rightText: for with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.

units.leftText: It is just as the Scripture says: “Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
units.rightText: For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be put to shame.

units.leftText: For there is no difference between Jew and Greek: The same Lord is Lord of all, and gives richly to all who call on Him,
units.rightText: For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek: for the same Lord is Lord of all, and is rich unto all that call upon him:

units.leftText: for, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”
units.rightText: for, Whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.

units.leftText: How then can they call on the One in whom they have not believed? And how can they believe in the One of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone to preach?
units.rightText: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?

units.leftText: And how can they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
units.rightText: and how shall they preach, except they be sent? even as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that bring glad tidings of good things!
leftNotes: 10:15 Literally good news of good things; BYZ and TR How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news of peace, who bring good news of good things; Isaiah 52:7|ISA 52:7*

units.leftText: But not all of them welcomed the good news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our message?”
units.rightText: But they did not all hearken to the glad tidings. For Isaiah saith, Lord, who hath believed our report?

units.leftText: Consequently, faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.
units.rightText: So belief cometh of hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.

units.leftText: But I ask, did they not hear? Indeed they did: “Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.”
units.rightText: But I say, Did they not hear? Yea, verily, Their sound went out into all the earth, And their words unto the ends of the world.

units.leftText: I ask instead, did Israel not understand? First, Moses says: “I will make you jealous by those who are not a nation; I will make you angry by a nation without understanding.”
units.rightText: But I say, Did Israel not know? First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy with that which is no nation, With a nation void of understanding will I anger you.

units.leftText: And Isaiah boldly says: “I was found by those who did not seek Me; I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me.”
units.rightText: And Isaiah is very bold, and saith, I was found of them that sought me not; I became manifest unto them that asked not of me.

units.leftText: But as for Israel he says: “All day long I have held out My hands to a disobedient and obstinate people.”
units.rightText: But as to Israel he saith, All the day long did I spread out my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people.

units.leftText: I ask then, did God reject His people? Certainly not! I am an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.
units.rightText: I say then, Did God cast off his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

units.leftText: God did not reject His people, whom He foreknew. Do you not know what the Scripture says about Elijah, how he appealed to God against Israel:
units.rightText: God did not cast off his people which he foreknew. Or know ye not what the scripture saith of Elijah? how he pleadeth with God against Israel:

units.leftText: “Lord, they have killed Your prophets and torn down Your altars. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well” ?
units.rightText: Lord, they have killed thy prophets, they have digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life.

units.leftText: And what was the divine reply to him? “I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”
units.rightText: But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have left for myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to Baal.

units.leftText: In the same way, at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.
units.rightText: Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.

units.leftText: And if it is by grace, then it is no longer by works. Otherwise, grace would no longer be grace.
units.rightText: But if it is by grace, it is no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace.
leftNotes: 11:6 BYZ and TR include But if it is by works, then it is no longer grace; otherwise work is no longer work.

units.leftText: What then? What Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain, but the elect did. The others were hardened,
units.rightText: What then? That which Israel seeketh for, that he obtained not; but the election obtained it, and the rest were hardened:

units.leftText: as it is written: “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that could not see, and ears that could not hear, to this very day.”
units.rightText: according as it is written, God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, unto this very day.

units.leftText: And David says: “May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution to them.
units.rightText: And David saith, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, And a stumblingblock, and a recompense unto them:

units.leftText: May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.” The Ingrafting of the Gentiles
units.rightText: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, And bow thou down their back always.

units.leftText: I ask then, did they stumble so as to fall beyond recovery? Certainly not! However, because of their trespass, salvation has come to the Gentiles to make Israel jealous.
units.rightText: I say then, Did they stumble that they might fall? God forbid: but by their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.
leftNotes: 11:11 Or did they stumble so as to lose their share? Literally did they stumble that they might fall?

units.leftText: But if their trespass means riches for the world, and their failure means riches for the Gentiles, how much greater riches will their fullness bring!
units.rightText: Now if their fall is the riches of the world, and their loss the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fulness?

units.leftText: I am speaking to you Gentiles. Inasmuch as I am the apostle to the Gentiles, I magnify my ministry
units.rightText: But I speak to you that are Gentiles. Inasmuch then as I am an apostle of Gentiles, I glorify my ministry;
