units.leftText: in the hope that I may provoke my own people to jealousy and save some of them.
units.rightText: if by any means I may provoke to jealousy them that are my flesh, and may save some of them.

units.leftText: For if their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?
units.rightText: For if the casting away of them is the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead?

units.leftText: If the first part of the dough is holy, so is the whole batch; if the root is holy, so are the branches.
units.rightText: And if the firstfruit is holy, so is the lump: and if the root is holy, so are the branches.

units.leftText: Now if some branches have been broken off, and you, a wild olive shoot, have been grafted in among the others to share in the nourishment of the olive root,
units.rightText: But if some of the branches were broken off, and thou, being a wild olive, wast grafted in among them, and didst become partaker with them of the root of the fatness of the olive tree;

units.leftText: do not boast over those branches. If you do, remember this: You do not support the root, but the root supports you.
units.rightText: glory not over the branches: but if thou gloriest, it is not thou that bearest the root, but the root thee.

units.leftText: You will say then, “Branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in.”
units.rightText: Thou wilt say then, Branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in.

units.leftText: That is correct: They were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not be arrogant, but be afraid.
units.rightText: Well; by their unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by thy faith. Be not highminded, but fear:

units.leftText: For if God did not spare the natural branches, He will certainly not spare you either.
units.rightText: for if God spared not the natural branches, neither will he spare thee.
leftNotes: 11:21 Or He will perhaps not; SBL, NE, and WH He will not

units.leftText: Take notice, therefore, of the kindness and severity of God: severity to those who fell, but kindness to you, if you continue in His kindness. Otherwise you also will be cut off.
units.rightText: Behold then the goodness and severity of God: toward them that fell, severity; but toward thee, God’s goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off.

units.leftText: And if they do not persist in unbelief, they will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.
units.rightText: And they also, if they continue not in their unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again.

units.leftText: For if you were cut from a wild olive tree, and contrary to nature were grafted into one that is cultivated, how much more readily will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree! All Israel Will Be Saved
units.rightText: For if thou wast cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and wast grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree; how much more shall these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?

units.leftText: I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, brothers, so that you will not be conceited: A hardening in part has come to Israel, until the full number of the Gentiles has come in.
units.rightText: For I would not, brethren, have you ignorant of this mystery, lest ye be wise in your own conceits, that a hardening in part hath befallen Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in;

units.leftText: And so all Israel will be saved, as it is written: “The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will remove godlessness from Jacob.
units.rightText: and so all Israel shall be saved: even as it is written, There shall come out of Zion the Deliverer; He shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob:

units.leftText: And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins.”
units.rightText: And this is my covenant unto them, When I shall take away their sins.
leftNotes: 11:27 Isaiah 27:9|ISA 27:9* and Isaiah 59:20–21; see also LXX

units.leftText: Regarding the gospel, they are enemies on your account; but regarding election, they are loved on account of the patriarchs.
units.rightText: As touching the gospel, they are enemies for your sake: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sake.

units.leftText: For God’s gifts and His call are irrevocable.
units.rightText: For the gifts and the calling of God are not repented of.

units.leftText: Just as you who formerly disobeyed God have now received mercy through their disobedience,
units.rightText: For as ye in time past were disobedient to God, but now have obtained mercy by their disobedience,

units.leftText: so they too have now disobeyed, in order that they too may now receive mercy through the mercy shown to you.
units.rightText: even so have these also now been disobedient, that by the mercy shown to you they also may now obtain mercy.
leftNotes: 11:31 Literally may now receive mercy through your mercy; BYZ and TR may receive mercy through your mercy

units.leftText: For God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone. A Hymn of Praise (Isaiah 40:9–31|ISA 40:9-31*)
units.rightText: For God hath shut up all unto disobedience, that he might have mercy upon all.

units.leftText: O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!
units.rightText: O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and the knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past tracing out!

units.leftText: “Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?”
units.rightText: For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been his counsellor?

units.leftText: “Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?”
units.rightText: or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again?

units.leftText: For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever! Amen.
units.rightText: For of him, and through him, and unto him, are all things. To him be the glory for ever. Amen.

units.leftText: Therefore I urge you, brothers, on account of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.
units.rightText: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service.

units.leftText: Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.
units.rightText: And be not fashioned according to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is the good and acceptable and perfect will of God.

units.leftText: For by the grace given me I say to every one of you: Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think of yourself with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has given you.
units.rightText: For I say, through the grace that was given me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but so to think as to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to each man a measure of faith.

units.leftText: Just as each of us has one body with many members, and not all members have the same function,
units.rightText: For even as we have many members in one body, and all the members have not the same office:

units.leftText: so in Christ we who are many are one body, and each member belongs to one another.
units.rightText: so we, who are many, are one body in Christ, and severally members one of another.

units.leftText: We have different gifts according to the grace given us. If one’s gift is prophecy, let him use it in proportion to his faith;
units.rightText: And having gifts differing according to the grace that was given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of our faith;

units.leftText: if it is serving, let him serve; if it is teaching, let him teach;
units.rightText: or ministry, let us give ourselves to our ministry; or he that teacheth, to his teaching;

units.leftText: if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is giving, let him give generously; if it is leading, let him lead with diligence; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully. Love, Zeal, Hope, Hospitality (John 13:31–35|JHN 13:31-35*; 1 John 3:11–24|1JN 3:11-24*)
units.rightText: or he that exhorteth, to his exhorting: he that giveth, let him do it with liberality; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that showeth mercy, with cheerfulness.

units.leftText: Love must be sincere. Detest what is evil; cling to what is good.
units.rightText: Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.

units.leftText: Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo yourselves in honoring one another.
units.rightText: In love of the brethren be tenderly affectioned one to another; in honor preferring one another;

units.leftText: Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.
units.rightText: in diligence not slothful; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;

units.leftText: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.
units.rightText: rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing stedfastly in prayer;

units.leftText: Share with the saints who are in need. Practice hospitality. Forgiveness (Matthew 18:21–35|MAT 18:21-35*)
units.rightText: communicating to the necessities of the saints; given to hospitality.

units.leftText: Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.
units.rightText: Bless them that persecute you; bless, and curse not.

units.leftText: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
units.rightText: Rejoice with them that rejoice; weep with them that weep.

units.leftText: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but associate with the lowly. Do not be conceited.
units.rightText: Be of the same mind one toward another. Set not your mind on high things, but condescend to things that are lowly. Be not wise in your own conceits.

units.leftText: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.
units.rightText: Render to no man evil for evil. Take thought for things honorable in the sight of all men.

units.leftText: If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.
units.rightText: If it be possible, as much as in you lieth, be at peace with all men.

units.leftText: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
units.rightText: Avenge not yourselves, beloved, but give place unto the wrath of God: for it is written, Vengeance belongeth unto me; I will recompense, saith the Lord.

units.leftText: On the contrary, “If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.”
units.rightText: But if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him to drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head.

units.leftText: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
units.rightText: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.

units.leftText: Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.
units.rightText: Let every soul be in subjection to the higher powers: for there is no power but of God; and the powers that be are ordained of God.

units.leftText: Consequently, whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place, and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves.
units.rightText: Therefore he that resisteth the power, withstandeth the ordinance of God: and they that withstand shall receive to themselves judgment.

units.leftText: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority? Then do what is right, and you will have his approval.
units.rightText: For rulers are not a terror to the good work, but to the evil. And wouldest thou have no fear of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise from the same:

units.leftText: For he is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword in vain. He is God’s servant, an agent of retribution to the wrongdoer.
units.rightText: for he is a minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is a minister of God, an avenger for wrath to him that doeth evil.

units.leftText: Therefore it is necessary to submit to authority, not only to avoid punishment, but also as a matter of conscience.
units.rightText: Wherefore ye must needs be in subjection, not only because of the wrath, but also for conscience’ sake.

units.leftText: This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.
units.rightText: For for this cause ye pay tribute also; for they are ministers of God’s service, attending continually upon this very thing.

units.leftText: Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due. Love Fulfills the Law (Leviticus 19:9–18|LEV 19:9-18*)
units.rightText: Render to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honor to whom honor.

units.leftText: Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.
units.rightText: Owe no man anything, save to love one another: for he that loveth his neighbor hath fulfilled the law.

units.leftText: The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
units.rightText: For this, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not covet, and if there be any other commandment, it is summed up in this word, namely, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.

units.leftText: Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law. The Day Is Near
units.rightText: Love worketh no ill to his neighbor: love therefore is the fulfilment of the law.

units.leftText: And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.
units.rightText: And this, knowing the season, that already it is time for you to awake out of sleep: for now is salvation nearer to us than when we first believed.

units.leftText: The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near. So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.
units.rightText: The night is far spent, and the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armor of light.

units.leftText: Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.
units.rightText: Let us walk becomingly, as in the day; not in revelling and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness, not in strife and jealousy.

units.leftText: Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.
units.rightText: But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.

units.leftText: Accept him whose faith is weak, without passing judgment on his opinions.
units.rightText: But him that is weak in faith receive ye, yet not for decision of scruples.
leftNotes: 14:1 Or without quarreling over disputable matters

units.leftText: For one person has faith to eat all things, while another, who is weak, eats only vegetables.
units.rightText: One man hath faith to eat all things: but he that is weak eateth herbs.

units.leftText: The one who eats everything must not belittle the one who does not, and the one who does not eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted him.
units.rightText: Let not him that eateth set at nought him that eateth not; and let not him that eateth not judge him that eateth: for God hath received him.

units.leftText: Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. And he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.
units.rightText: Who art thou that judgest the servant of another? to his own lord he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be made to stand; for the Lord hath power to make him stand.

units.leftText: One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.
units.rightText: One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day alike. Let each man be fully assured in his own mind.

units.leftText: He who observes a special day does so to the Lord; he who eats does so to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and he who abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.
units.rightText: He that regardeth the day, regardeth it unto the Lord: and he that eateth, eateth unto the Lord, for he giveth God thanks; and he that eateth not, unto the Lord he eateth not, and giveth God thanks.
leftNotes: 14:6 BYZ and TR include he who does not regard the day, to the Lord he does not regard it;

units.leftText: For none of us lives to himself alone, and none of us dies to himself alone.
units.rightText: For none of us liveth to himself, and none dieth to himself.

units.leftText: If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
units.rightText: For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; or whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord’s.

units.leftText: For this reason Christ died and returned to life, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.
units.rightText: For to this end Christ died and lived again, that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living.

units.leftText: Why, then, do you judge your brother? Or why do you belittle your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat.
units.rightText: But thou, why dost thou judge thy brother? or thou again, why dost thou set at nought thy brother? for we shall all stand before the judgment-seat of God.

units.leftText: It is written: “As surely as I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow before Me; every tongue will confess to God.”
units.rightText: For it is written, As I live, saith the Lord, to me every knee shall bow, And every tongue shall confess to God.
leftNotes: 14:11 Or will give praise to God or will acknowledge God; Isaiah 45:23|ISA 45:23* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God. The Law of Love (Ezekiel 14:1–11|EZK 14:1-11*; 1 Corinthians 8:1–13|1CO 8:1-13*)
units.rightText: So then each one of us shall give account of himself to God.

units.leftText: Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s way.
units.rightText: Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge ye this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock in his brother’s way, or an occasion of falling.

units.leftText: I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.
units.rightText: I know, and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus, that nothing is unclean of itself: save that to him who accounteth anything to be unclean, to him it is unclean.

units.leftText: If your brother is distressed by what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy your brother, for whom Christ died.
units.rightText: For if because of meat thy brother is grieved, thou walkest no longer in love. Destroy not with thy meat him for whom Christ died.

units.leftText: Do not allow what you consider good, then, to be spoken of as evil.
units.rightText: Let not then your good be evil spoken of:

units.leftText: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: for the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: For whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by men.
units.rightText: For he that herein serveth Christ is well-pleasing to God, and approved of men.

units.leftText: So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.
units.rightText: So then let us follow after things which make for peace, and things whereby we may edify one another.

units.leftText: Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a man to let his eating be a stumbling block.
units.rightText: Overthrow not for meat’s sake the work of God. All things indeed are clean; howbeit it is evil for that man who eateth with offence.

units.leftText: It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything to cause your brother to stumble.
units.rightText: It is good not to eat flesh, nor to drink wine, nor to do anything whereby thy brother stumbleth.
leftNotes: 14:21 SBL, BYZ, and TR include or to be hindered or weakened.

units.leftText: Keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.
units.rightText: The faith which thou hast, have thou to thyself before God. Happy is he that judgeth not himself in that which he approveth.
leftNotes: 14:22 Literally Keep the faith that you have to yourself before God

units.leftText: But the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.
units.rightText: But he that doubteth is condemned if he eat, because he eateth not of faith; and whatsoever is not of faith is sin.
leftNotes: 14:23 Some manuscripts place the text of Romans 16:25–27|ROM 16:25-27* here.

units.leftText: We who are strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves.
units.rightText: Now we that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to please ourselves.

units.leftText: Each of us should please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.
units.rightText: Let each one of us please his neighbor for that which is good, unto edifying.

units.leftText: For even Christ did not please Himself, but as it is written: “The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.”
units.rightText: For Christ also pleased not himself; but, as it is written, The reproaches of them that reproached thee fell upon me.

units.leftText: For everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.
units.rightText: For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that through patience and through comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.

units.leftText: Now may the God who gives endurance and encouragement grant you harmony with one another in Christ Jesus,
units.rightText: Now the God of patience and of comfort grant you to be of the same mind one with another according to Christ Jesus:

units.leftText: so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. Christ the Servant of Jews and Gentiles
units.rightText: that with one accord ye may with one mouth glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.
units.rightText: Wherefore receive ye one another, even as Christ also received you, to the glory of God.

units.leftText: For I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the circumcised on behalf of God’s truth, to confirm the promises made to the patriarchs,
units.rightText: For I say that Christ hath been made a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God, that he might confirm the promises given unto the fathers,

units.leftText: so that the Gentiles may glorify God for His mercy. As it is written: “Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles; I will sing hymns to Your name.”
units.rightText: and that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy; as it is written, Therefore will I give praise unto thee among the Gentiles, And sing unto thy name.

units.leftText: Again, it says: “Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people.”
units.rightText: And again he saith, Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people.

units.leftText: And again: “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and extol Him, all you peoples.”
units.rightText: And again, Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles; And let all the peoples praise him.

units.leftText: And once more, Isaiah says: “The Root of Jesse will appear, One who will arise to rule over the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will put their hope.”
units.rightText: And again, Isaiah saith, There shall be the root of Jesse, And he that ariseth to rule over the Gentiles; On him shall the Gentiles hope.

units.leftText: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe in Him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit. Paul the Minister to the Gentiles
units.rightText: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, in the power of the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: I myself am convinced, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, brimming with knowledge, and able to instruct one another.
units.rightText: And I myself also am persuaded of you, my brethren, that ye yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another.

units.leftText: However, I have written you a bold reminder on some points, because of the grace God has given me
units.rightText: But I write the more boldly unto you in some measure, as putting you again in remembrance, because of the grace that was given me of God,

units.leftText: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: that I should be a minister of Christ Jesus unto the Gentiles, ministering the gospel of God, that the offering up of the Gentiles might be made acceptable, being sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: Therefore I exult in Christ Jesus in my service to God.
units.rightText: I have therefore my glorying in Christ Jesus in things pertaining to God.

units.leftText: I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me in leading the Gentiles to obedience by word and deed,
units.rightText: For I will not dare to speak of any things save those which Christ wrought through me, for the obedience of the Gentiles, by word and deed,

units.leftText: by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.
units.rightText: in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Holy Spirit; so that from Jerusalem, and round about even unto Illyricum, I have fully preached the gospel of Christ;
leftNotes: 15:19 SBL the power of the Spirit; NE and WH the power of the Holy Spirit

units.leftText: In this way I have aspired to preach the gospel where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else’s foundation.
units.rightText: yea, making it my aim so to preach the gospel, not where Christ was already named, that I might not build upon another man’s foundation;

units.leftText: Rather, as it is written: “Those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”
units.rightText: but, as it is written, They shall see, to whom no tidings of him came, And they who have not heard shall understand.

units.leftText: That is why I have often been hindered from coming to you. Paul’s Travel Plans (1 Corinthians 16:5–9|1CO 16:5-9*)
units.rightText: Wherefore also I was hindered these many times from coming to you:

units.leftText: But now that there are no further opportunities for me in these regions, and since I have longed for many years to visit you,
units.rightText: but now, having no more any place in these regions, and having these many years a longing to come unto you,

units.leftText: I hope to see you on my way to Spain. And after I have enjoyed your company for a while, you can equip me for my journey.
units.rightText: whensoever I go unto Spain (for I hope to see you in my journey, and to be brought on my way thitherward by you, if first in some measure I shall have been satisfied with your company)—

units.leftText: Now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem to serve the saints there.
units.rightText: but now, I say, I go unto Jerusalem, ministering unto the saints.

units.leftText: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: For it hath been the good pleasure of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor among the saints that are at Jerusalem.

units.leftText: They were pleased to do it, and indeed they owe it to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual blessings, they are obligated to minister to them with material blessings.
units.rightText: Yea, it hath been their good pleasure; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, they owe it to them also to minister unto them in carnal things.

units.leftText: So after I have completed this service and have safely delivered this bounty to them, I will set off to Spain by way of you.
units.rightText: When therefore I have accomplished this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will go on by you unto Spain.

units.leftText: I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
units.rightText: And I know that, when I come unto you, I shall come in the fulness of the blessing of Christ.
leftNotes: 15:29 TR and BYZ include of the gospel.

units.leftText: Now I urge you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join me in my struggle by praying to God for me.
units.rightText: Now I beseech you, brethren, by our Lord Jesus Christ, and by the love of the Spirit, that ye strive together with me in your prayers to God for me;

units.leftText: Pray that I may be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints there,
units.rightText: that I may be delivered from them that are disobedient in Judæa, and that my ministration which I have for Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints;

units.leftText: so that by God’s will I may come to you with joy and together with you be refreshed.
units.rightText: that I may come unto you in joy through the will of God, and together with you find rest.

units.leftText: The God of peace be with all of you. Amen.
units.rightText: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
leftNotes: 15:33 Some manuscripts do not include Amen.One early manuscript places the text of Romans 16:25–27|ROM 16:25-27* here.

units.leftText: I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea.
units.rightText: I commend unto you Phoebe our sister, who is a servant of the church that is at Cenchreæ:

units.leftText: Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her with anything she may need from you. For she has been a great help to many people, including me.
units.rightText: that ye receive her in the Lord, worthily of the saints, and that ye assist her in whatsoever matter she may have need of you: for she herself also hath been a helper of many, and of mine own self.

units.leftText: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
units.rightText: Salute Prisca and Aquila my fellow-workers in Christ Jesus,
leftNotes: 16:3 Prisca is a variant of Priscilla; see Acts 18:2|ACT 18:2*.

units.leftText: who have risked their lives for me. Not only I but all the churches of the Gentiles are grateful to them.
units.rightText: who for my life laid down their own necks; unto whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles:

units.leftText: Greet also the church that meets at their house. Greet my beloved Epenetus, who was the first convert to Christ in the province of Asia.
units.rightText: and salute the church that is in their house. Salute Epænetus my beloved, who is the firstfruits of Asia unto Christ.
leftNotes: 16:5 Literally in Asia; Asia was a Roman province in what is now western Turkey.

units.leftText: Greet Mary, who has worked very hard for you.
units.rightText: Salute Mary, who bestowed much labor on you.

units.leftText: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my fellow countrymen and fellow prisoners. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before I was.
units.rightText: Salute Andronicus and Junias, my kinsmen, and my fellow-prisoners, who are of note among the apostles, who also have been in Christ before me.

units.leftText: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
units.rightText: Salute Ampliatus my beloved in the Lord.

units.leftText: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my beloved Stachys.
units.rightText: Salute Urbanus our fellow-worker in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.

units.leftText: Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ. Greet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.
units.rightText: Salute Apelles the approved in Christ. Salute them that are of the household of Aristobulus.

units.leftText: Greet Herodion, my fellow countryman. Greet those from the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
units.rightText: Salute Herodion my kinsman. Salute them of the household of Narcissus, that are in the Lord.

units.leftText: Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, women who have worked hard in the Lord. Greet my beloved Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.
units.rightText: Salute Tryphæna and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Salute Persis the beloved, who labored much in the Lord.

units.leftText: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me as well.
units.rightText: Salute Rufus the chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

units.leftText: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
units.rightText: Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brethren that are with them.

units.leftText: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.
units.rightText: Salute Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints that are with them.

units.leftText: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ send you greetings. Avoid Divisions (Titus 3:9–11|TIT 3:9-11*)
units.rightText: Salute one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ salute you.

units.leftText: Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles that are contrary to the teaching you have learned. Turn away from them.
units.rightText: Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them that are causing the divisions and occasions of stumbling, contrary to the doctrine which ye learned: and turn away from them.

units.leftText: For such people are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive.
units.rightText: For they that are such serve not our Lord Christ, but their own belly; and by their smooth and fair speech they beguile the hearts of the innocent.

units.leftText: Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.
units.rightText: For your obedience is come abroad unto all men. I rejoice therefore over you: but I would have you wise unto that which is good, and simple unto that which is evil.

units.leftText: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Greetings from Paul’s Fellow Workers (Colossians 4:7–14|COL 4:7-14*)
units.rightText: And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
leftNotes: 16:20 NA, NE, and WH Lord Jesus

units.leftText: Timothy, my fellow worker, sends you greetings, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my fellow countrymen.
units.rightText: Timothy my fellow-worker saluteth you; and Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my kinsmen.

units.leftText: I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.
units.rightText: I Tertius, who write the epistle, salute you in the Lord.

units.leftText: Gaius, who has hosted me and all the church, sends you greetings. Erastus, the city treasurer, sends you greetings, as does our brother Quartus. Doxology (Jude 1:24–25|JUD 24-25*)
units.rightText: Gaius my host, and of the whole church, saluteth you. Erastus the treasurer of the city saluteth you, and Quartus the brother.
leftNotes: 16:23 SBL, BYZ, and TR include 24*May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

rightNotes: 16:24 Some ancient authorities insert here v. 24 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen, and omit the like words in v. 20.

units.leftText: Now to Him who is able to strengthen you by my gospel and by the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery concealed for ages past
units.rightText: Now to him that is able to establish you according to my gospel and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery which hath been kept in silence through times eternal,

units.leftText: but now revealed and made known through the writings of the prophets by the command of the eternal God, in order to lead all nations to the obedience that comes from faith —
units.rightText: but now is manifested, and by the scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the eternal God, is made known unto all the nations unto obedience of faith:

units.leftText: to the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ! Amen.
units.rightText: to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory for ever. Amen.
leftNotes: 16:27 Some manuscripts place the text of verses 25–27 after Romans 14:23|ROM 14:23* or after Romans 15:33.
